purpose: Curated, deduplicated, quality-filtered sample from a published NFR classification dataset, remapped to this project's 13-category taxonomy. Covers the 4 categories with direct 1:1 analogs (Security, Usability, Performance, Operational). Intended to supplement -- not replace -- the finance-domain manual/synthetic training data, since these examples are NOT from BFSI scenarios.

provenance.original_dataset: PROMISE NFR dataset (and its common derivatives)
provenance.citation: Cleland-Huang, J., Settimi, R., Zou, X., & Solc, P. (2007). Automated classification of non-functional requirements. Requirements Engineering, 12(2), 103-120. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00766-007-0045-1
processing_applied: Dropped the 'Maintainability' class -- no analog in this project's 13-category taxonomy
Removed statements shorter than 6 or longer than 32 words

Removed statements lacking requirement modal language (shall/must/should/will/etc.) or containing technical-instruction noise (e.g. literal command syntax) -- several rows in the raw file were how-to snippets or fragments, not real requirement statements
Stratified random sample of 15 per category (seed=42) from the cleaned pool

instructions_for_reviewers: These are lighter-review than the fully synthetic set: category label already comes from a peer-reviewed, expert-annotated source.

Still confirm each one reads naturally as a requirement and fits the category as YOUR project defines it -- some NFR taxonomies define 'Security' or 'Operational' slightly differently than PROMISE did.

These are NOT finance-domain (mixed real estate, healthcare, campus-system, retail SRS docs). Recommend capping this external set to well under half of the final per-category training count, so finance vocabulary still dominates what the classifier sees.
Cite the original PROMISE NFR paper in your Month 4 documentation, not just the GitHub mirror, since that's the actual source of the annotation.
